#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# watchdog_trip_check.sh — the gh-2290 timeout-kill trip decision for the
# `watchdog` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml (issue #194 point 4).
#
# The watchdog's remedy for a degraded-runner allocation is ONE retrigger
# with a fresh allocation (never `gh run rerun`). Tripping requires
# recognizing a job-level timeout KILL — and only that kill. The v1.0.745
# tag run 4424840840 hung a PTY shard (the pty2 blocking-waitpid wedge,
# `Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in`), burned
# its 40-minute budget and was killed by `timeout-minutes`: GitHub landed
# that kill as job conclusion `cancelled` (NOT `failure` — jobs
# 134588877581/134566192421) with the mid-flight step `cancelled` and the
# trailing `if: always()` evidence steps `skipped`.
#
# gh-2358 added the SECOND kill shape: runner DEATH. The v1.0.759 tag run
# (44868070949, job 136736814346) lost its self-hosted runner `fa-m5-1`
# ~11 minutes into `flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)` ("The
# self-hosted runner lost communication with the server"). GitHub
# concluded the JOB `failure` but NOTHING ever reported again: the
# mid-flight step — and every trailing step — froze at conclusion `null`,
# so the `cancelled`-step-only signature was blind to it. The watchdog
# ran, found nothing, and the release train sat red (no GitHub release,
# `vpinned` marker stuck) until a manual full rerun. One trip decision,
# two kill shapes: the mid-flight cut is `cancelled` (GitHub concluded
# the cancel) or `null` (nothing ever concluded).
#
# The degraded-runner-kill signature, as one predicate over the jobs JSON:
#
#   job conclusion == "failure" OR "cancelled"      (both kill shapes land)
#   AND at least one step concluded "cancelled" OR "null"
#     (a step was cut mid-flight — the kill itself; `null` is the
#     frozen runner-death tail, gh-2358)
#   AND NO step concluded "failure"                  (a real test failure
#     ENDS with a failed step — in these shards the `if: always()`
#     evidence steps often trail it with `success` — so a genuine red
#     never trips; a fresh runner allocation cannot fix a defect. This
#     guard also covers death AFTER a real red: the failed step is
#     concluded, only the trailing steps freeze at `null`)
#
# A cancelled job with NO steps (never started — a run-level cancel
# reaching a queued job) is NOT a kill (`any()` over an empty steps
# array is false). Success/skipped never trip. A job whose conclusion
# is still null is in flight — the first select filters it out, so an
# in-progress leg can never fake the signature.
#
# Network-free by contract: the caller fetches the run's jobs document in
# ONE call (the jobs API embeds each job's steps array — `gh run view
# --json jobs`; `gh api .../runs/<id>/jobs` is fine unpaged, but
# `--paginate` concatenates page bodies and jq then reads only the first
# page — verified against a 69-job run) and hands the FILE here.
# Fixture-self-tested by scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh (#1100
# pattern), wired into the static gate; the workflow wiring is pinned by
# test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart.
#
# Usage: watchdog_trip_check.sh [jobs-json-file] [output-file]
#   jobs-json-file  the jobs document; `-` or an empty arg reads stdin
#   output-file     default $GITHUB_OUTPUT when set (the trip=<bool> line
#                   lands there AND on stdout); without one, stdout only.
#                   Diagnostics never start with `trip=`, so the line is
#                   unambiguous in both sinks.
set -u

json_file="${1:--}"
out_file="${2:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-}}"

if [ "$json_file" = "-" ] || [ -z "$json_file" ]; then
  jobs_json="$(cat)"
else
  jobs_json="$(cat "$json_file")"
fi

# The degraded-runner-kill signature, as ONE shared jq filter (the count
# and the diagnostics below project over the same filter — a duplicated
# literal can drift silently, and the selftest pins only the trip=
# contract): failed-or-cancelled jobs with a mid-flight cut (>=1 step
# concluded `cancelled` OR frozen unconcluded `null`) and NO failed step.
filter='.jobs[]?
   | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
   | select(any(.steps[]?; .conclusion == "cancelled" or .conclusion == null))
   | select(all(.steps[]?; .conclusion != "failure"))'

matches="$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "[$filter] | length")"

if [ -z "$matches" ] || ! [ "$matches" -eq "$matches" ] 2>/dev/null; then
  # A malformed projection must NEVER flip the trip (fail-safe: the
  # watchdog is an optimization — a broken pre-check degrades to no
  # retrigger, never to a spurious dispatch loop).
  echo "::warning::watchdog_trip_check: unparseable jobs JSON or jq failure — not tripping"
  matches=0
fi

trip=false
if [ "$matches" -gt 0 ]; then
  trip=true
fi

if [ "$trip" = "true" ]; then
  echo "::notice::watchdog_trip_check: $matches job(s) match the degraded-runner-kill signature (gh-2290/gh-2358):"
  printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "[$filter]
    | (.[] | \"  \" + .name + \": \" + .conclusion
       + \" (mid-flight cut: \"
       + ([.steps[]? | select(.conclusion == \"cancelled\" or .conclusion == null) | .name] | join(\", \"))
       + \")\")
  "
else
  echo "watchdog_trip_check: no degraded-runner-kill signature — nothing to retrigger"
fi

if [ -n "$out_file" ]; then
  {
    printf 'trip=%s\n' "$trip"
  } >> "$out_file"
fi
echo "trip=$trip"

#

# trip decision (scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh, the `watchdog` job in

#
# The v1.0.745 tag run (4424840840) hung a PTY shard on the pty2
# blocking-waitpid wedge (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode
# to check in`), burned its whole 40-minute budget, was concluded
# `cancelled` — and NOTHING retrigged: the watchdog was pull_request-only
# AND its detector scanned failure-conclusion jobs only. The decision must
# trip exactly on the timeout-kill signature and never on a genuine red.
# Proves, on fixture JSON (no network, no gh, no token):
#   AC1  the gh-2290 kill mode: job conclusion `cancelled`, the
#     mid-flight step `cancelled`, trailing `if: always()` evidence
#     steps `skipped` — the EXACT shape of hung shard jobs
#     134588877581/134566192421 → trip,
#   AC2  the classic kill mode: job `failure`, a cut `cancelled` step,
#     no failed step → trip,
#   AC3  the gh-2358 runner-death kill mode: the box (fa-m5-1, v1.0.759
#     tag run 44868070949, job 136736814346) lost communication ~11 min
#     into `flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)`; the JOB concluded
#     `failure` and the mid-flight step — with every trailing step —
#     froze at conclusion `null` (never reported). One trip decision,
#     two kill shapes: the mid-flight cut is `cancelled` (GitHub
#     concluded the cancel) or `null` (nothing ever concluded).
#   FC1  a REAL test failure never trips — in either landing shape: the
#     failed step LAST, or the failed step TRAILED by the `if: always()`
#     evidence steps (`success`) that every red pty shard actually
#     leaves behind (last-step-success — the old last-step detector was
#     blind to this too),
#   FC2  success / skipped / a cancelled never-started job (no steps) /
#     an empty jobs array never trip,
#   FC3  a malformed body fails SAFE to trip=false with a warning (a
#     broken pre-check must degrade to no retrigger, never to a
#     spurious dispatch loop),
#   FC4  the runner died AFTER a real test failure — the red step
#     concluded `failure` and only the trailing steps froze at `null`:
#     a genuine red must never trip, regardless of the frozen tail.
#   RG   the output contract: exactly ONE `trip=<bool>` line, no
#     diagnostic masquerading as `trip=`, GITHUB_OUTPUT lands exactly
#     one line, multiple matches still produce a single line, and the
#     stdin arm (`-`) works.
# Same discipline as release_dedupe_selftest.sh (gh-1625, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/watchdog_trip_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

fixture() { # fixture <name> <json> — write a fixture, run the check
  _fx_name="$1"; shift
  printf '%s' "$1" > "$TMP/$_fx_name.json"
  bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/$_fx_name.json" 2>&1
}

trip_line() { # trip_line <output> — the trip= line, empty when absent
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -E '^trip=(true|false)$' | head -1
}

trip_count() { # trip_count <output> — number of trip= lines
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -cE '^trip=(true|false)$'
}

json_for() { # json_for <conclusion> <shape: kill|failure|success>
  # kill:    the REAL gh-2290 shape — the mid-flight dart test step
  #          cancelled, the trailing if:always() evidence steps skipped.
  # death:   the REAL gh-2358 runner-death shape — the mid-flight
  #          flutter build ios step and everything after it froze at
  #          conclusion null (the runner never reported anything again).
  # failure: a real test failure — the dart test step FAILED, the
  #          evidence steps still trail with success (the last step is
  #          NOT the failed one in these shards).
  # success: a clean job.
  case "$2" in
    kill)    steps='[{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "cancelled"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": "skipped"}, {"name": "upload artifact", "conclusion": "skipped"}, {"name": "Post cache", "conclusion": "skipped"}]' ;;
    death)   steps='[{"name": "flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)", "conclusion": null}, {"name": "Post Run ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get", "conclusion": null}, {"name": "Post Cache CocoaPods (iOS)", "conclusion": null}]' ;;
    failure) steps='[{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": "success"}]' ;;
    *)       steps='[{"name": "run", "conclusion": "success"}]' ;;
  esac
  cat <<JEOF
{"jobs": [{"name": "PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)", "conclusion": "$1", "steps": $steps}]}
JEOF
}

echo "watchdog_trip_selftest (gh-2290):"

# AC1 — the gh-2290 kill mode (the REAL shape: conclusion cancelled,
# mid-flight step cancelled, trailing always()-evidence steps skipped).
out="$(fixture ac1 "$(json_for cancelled kill)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC1 cancelled job with a cancelled step trips (gh-2290 kill mode)" $?

# AC2 — the classic kill mode (failure conclusion, cut step, no failed step).
out="$(fixture ac2 "$(json_for failure kill)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC2 failure job with a cancelled step and no failed step trips" $?

# AC3 — the gh-2358 runner-death kill mode (the REAL shape: fa-m5-1
# lost communication ~11 min into the flutter build ios step of tag
# run 44868070949, job 136736814346; the JOB concluded failure and the
# mid-flight step — with every trailing step — froze at null).
out="$(fixture ac3 "$(json_for failure death)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC3 failure job with an UNCONCLUDED (null) mid-flight step trips (gh-2358 runner death)" $?

# AC3b — the same runner death under the cancelled conclusion (a
# run-level cancel racing the lost heartbeat): still a mid-flight cut,
# still no failed step.
out="$(fixture ac3b "$(json_for cancelled death)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC3b cancelled job with an unconcluded (null) mid-flight step trips" $?

# FC1 — a real test failure must NOT retrigger (both landing shapes).
out="$(fixture fc1a '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 0/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit", "conclusion": "success"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC1a real test failure (failed step, trailing evidence) does NOT trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc1b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 3/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "setup", "conclusion": "success"}, {"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC1b real test failure (failed LAST step) does NOT trip" $?

# FC4 — the runner died AFTER a real test failure: the red step
# concluded `failure`, then the box vanished before the trailing
# always() evidence steps reported — they froze at null. A genuine red
# must never trip regardless of the frozen tail (a fresh runner
# allocation cannot fix a defect).
out="$(fixture fc4 '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 1/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": null}, {"name": "Post cache", "conclusion": null}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC4 failed step + frozen trailing steps (death after a real red) does NOT trip" $?

# FC2 — clean, skipped, never-started, empty.
out="$(fixture fc2a '{"jobs": [{"name": "Static gates", "conclusion": "success", "steps": [{"name": "analyze", "conclusion": "success"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2a success job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Golden suite (macOS baselines)", "conclusion": "skipped", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2b skipped job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2c '{"jobs": [{"name": "Binaries smoke gate", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2c cancelled never-started job (no steps) does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2d '{"jobs": []}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2d empty jobs array does not trip" $?

# FC3 — malformed body fails safe.
out="$(fixture fc3 'not json at all')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC3 malformed jobs JSON fails safe to trip=false" $?
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '::warning::'
check "FC3 malformed body warns loudly" $?

# RG — output contract.
out="$(fixture rg1 "$(json_for cancelled kill)")"
[ "$(trip_count "$out")" = "1" ]
check "RG1 exactly one trip= line on stdout" $?

printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -vE '^trip=' | grep -qE '^trip='
[ $? -ne 0 ]
check "RG2 no diagnostic line masquerades as trip=" $?

out_file="$TMP/github_output"
: > "$out_file"
GITHUB_OUTPUT="$out_file" bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/ac1.json" > "$TMP/rg3.out"
grep -cE '^trip=(true|false)$' "$out_file" > "$TMP/rg3.count"
[ "$(cat "$TMP/rg3.count")" = "1" ]
check "RG3 exactly one trip= line lands in GITHUB_OUTPUT" $?

out="$(fixture rg4 '{"jobs": [{"name": "PTY shard 2/3", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "cancelled"}, {"name": "upload", "conclusion": "skipped"}]}, {"name": "PTY shard 0/3", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "cancelled"}, {"name": "upload", "conclusion": "skipped"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
[ "$(trip_count "$out")" = "1" ]
check "RG4 multiple matches trip once, one line" $?

# RG5 — stdin arm (`-`).
out="$(printf '%s' "$(json_for cancelled kill)" | bash "$CHECK" - 2>&1)"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "RG5 stdin arm trips" $?

if [ "$fails" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "watchdog_trip_selftest: $fails FAILURE(S)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "watchdog_trip_selftest: all green"

The "Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in" message is not from the repo's own code nor from test_core/vm_service pub packages — it must be from the Dart VM itself (the runtime's exit handshake — `dart:isolate` exit at VM shutdown, printed by the VM when an isolate refuses to check in at a safepoint). The message format "Attempt:N waiting for isolate X to check in" is the Dart VM's `Isolate` exit-wait message (from `runtime/vm/isolate.cc` — "Attempt %d waiting for isolate %s to check in"). `PtyCoreUnixWorker.exitCodeBlocking()` calls `waitpid(pid, ..., 0)` — blocking. The ONLY ways it returns:
1. The child exits → waitpid returns pid → exit code.
2. ECHILD (pidResult < 0): the VM reaped the child first → checks `kill(pid, 0)` — if dead → return -1. **BUT if ECHILD and the child is somehow still alive... wait, ECHILD means not a child anymore, so `kill(pid,0)` succeeding means the pid is alive but not our child** (reparented? No — a child of THIS process can't be reparented unless it's a grandchild). Hmm — when would ECHILD fire while the process is alive? If waitpid is called for a pid that is NOT this process's child. E.g., pid 0 or -1 misuse, or the pid was never a child.

Actually more interesting: `waitpid(pid, ...)` blocking with a live child = blocks indefinitely. So `_waitForExitCode` isolate stays alive as long as the CHILD stays alive. A wedge at VM exit means the child process was STILL ALIVE when the test process tried to exit.

Now — who is the child? The pty2 spawn: let me look at how PtyCoreUnix spawns the child (fork/exec of what?). Let me read the spawn function and `open`/constructor for the shell used.

The harness spawns `fa` over the pty (bash -c wrapper?). Let me check pty_harness.dart spawn + close, and — importantly — which suites ran in shard 2/3. The junit artifact lists 80 testcases. Let me download the artifact to get the exact suite list, then figure out which suite could leave a live child after all its tests passed.

Unless... `harness.close` was NOT awaited or the tearDown ordering issue: `addTearDown(tempHome.deleteSync(recursive: true))` is registered BEFORE `addTearDown(harness.close)` — tearDowns run LIFO: harness.close first, then tempHome deletion. Fine.

BUT — what if `harness.close` (shutdownPty) leaves the child in a state where the child doesn't die? shutdownPty throws StateError if the child survives SIGKILL — the test would have FAILED then. All tests passed. So each test's own pty child was reaped.

The LEAK must be elsewhere: a child spawned NOT via a shutdownPty-wrapped path. Candidates:
1. `Process.start` / `Process.run` children of the test process (Dart `Process` children are reaped by the VM's own reaper; their exit doesn't involve pty2 isolates — they don't wedge the exit handshake; the VM reaps them).

Is the wedged isolate necessarily in the MAIN test process? `dart test` VM runner: each suite file runs in a separate ISOLATE of the same process (spawned via `Isolate.spawnUri`? no...). Hmm. In package:test's VM platform, suites are loaded by spawning a NEW PROCESS? No — I recall: `dart test` runs all suites as isolates within one "root" process by default when concurrency allows, but each suite gets its OWN ISOLATE (via `Isolate.spawn` of a bootstrap). pty2's `Isolate.spawn(_waitForExitCode)` inside a suite isolate creates an isolate in the SAME process (isolate groups share the process). The VM exit handshake waits for ALL isolates in the process. So yes — wedged `_waitForExitCode` in the main process.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fa --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p build/test-results
          # Issue #2331: same loopback-ws loader-drop family as the core
          # shards (occ1 + occ5 hit THIS leg at --concurrency=4 — the cap
          # alone does not kill the class). One-shot rerun of the dropped
          # file only; see scripts/load_drop_retry.sh.
          bash scripts/load_drop_retry.sh \
            "build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            "build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.retry.json" \
            -- \
            dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            "$targets"
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          build/test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/gh995_artifact_action_pins_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          # gh-2200: rerun --failed never fires the gh-1412 retry (the
          # first attempt's upload succeeded), so without this the rerun
          # uploads a SECOND same-named artifact and download-artifact
          # pattern-mode resolves the STALE previous-attempt report — the
          # pty-coverage-gate then merges a truncated shard json and
          # phantom-fails "budgeted suite did not run" (run 43752856871
          # attempt 2). The latest attempt's evidence must win.
          overwrite: true
      - name: Retry integration-json upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_json.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_integration_junit
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
          # gh-2200: same rerun-idempotency as upload_integration_json —
          # a rerun attempt must REPLACE its previous attempt's artifact,
          # never stack a stale duplicate beside it.
          overwrite: true
      - name: Retry junit upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_junit.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
          overwrite: true
      # coverage/ is written incrementally — a red leg still formats and
      # uploads so the gate below merges what ran.
      - name: Format coverage to lcov (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_pty_coverage
        if: always()
        with:
          name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          # gh-2200: same rerun-idempotency as upload_integration_json —
          # the coverage merge below must never read a previous attempt's
          # lcov through a stale same-named duplicate.
          overwrite: true
      - name: Retry coverage upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always() && steps.upload_pty_coverage.outcome == 'failure'

+  /// Bounded load-tolerant wait for a registry mutation's observable
+  /// effect — the same `_waitFor` shape as the shell-job drain suite:
+  /// 5ms polls up to 20s, then a LOUD fail naming the unreached state
+  /// (never a silent pass, never an unbounded sleep).
+  Future<void> waitForManifestId(
+    LocalExecutionEnv env,
+    String logs,
+    String id,
+  ) async {
+    for (var i = 0; i < 4000; i++) {
+      final text = (await env.readTextFile('$logs/running.json')).valueOrNull;
+      if (text != null && manifestIds(text).contains(id)) return;
+      await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 5));
+    }

+      'timed out waiting: the settle-side registry mutation never landed '
+      '$id in $logs/running.json',
+    );

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# load_drop_retry.sh — one-shot loopback-ws load-drop retry for sharded
# dart test legs (issue #2331).
#
# Family: under CI-leg load the dart test loader's loopback WebSocket
# (127.0.0.1:…/ws) to a freshly spawned test VM can die mid-handshake —
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection closed before full header was
#   received, uri = http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection reset by peer, uri=http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
# The victim file is arbitrary (whatever is loading when the socket dies),
# never an assertion failure (6/6 occurrences on the card). The shard reds
# even though every test that ran was green.
#
# This wrapper runs the shard's dart test command as given, and on failure
# that carries BOTH the `Failed to load "<path>"` marker AND a ws-drop
# signature, re-runs the failed inventory ONCE (the gh-1026
# rerun-only-failed-files discipline): the ws-dropped files PLUS every
# attempt-1 failed suite the main reporter log records (via the repo's
# scripts/gate_failed_targets.py). A co-occurring real failure — assertion
# failure or compile-error load failure — is therefore IN the rerun and
# keeps the shard red; an attempt 1 whose only failures are ws drops heals.
# Without the ws-drop signature the wrapper never reruns at all: real
# failures stay loud, nothing is rerun blind, nothing is masked.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/load_drop_retry.sh <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> "<targets>"
#
#   <main-log>   the path of the caller's own --file-reporter=json:<main-log>
#                (passed as part of <cmd...>) that junit/duration consumers
#                read — attempt-1 evidence is never clobbered; also names
#                the <main-log>.console capture;
#   <retry-log>  where the rerun's reporter writes (kept separate so the
#                main log is never overwritten);
#   <cmd...>     the full dart test invocation INCLUDING its own
#                --file-reporter flag; the FINAL argument is the quoted,
#                space-separated target list (word-split here).
#
# Exit: 0 when the run (or the single rerun) is green; the failing exit
# code otherwise. Coverage consumers are safe: the rerun inherits
# --coverage=coverage, so a healed file's hits land in the same coverage/
# dir the gate merges.
set -euo pipefail
# TARGETS/RERUN_TARGETS expand unquoted below (word-split by design — the
# caller passes a quoted, space-separated list). Glob-off: a path carrying
# glob metacharacters must never expand (PR #2347 review digest).
set -f

usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> \"<targets>\"" >&2
  exit 2
}

[ "$#" -ge 5 ] || usage
MAIN_LOG=$1
RETRY_LOG=$2
[ "${3:-}" = "--" ] || usage
shift 3
CMD=("${@:1:$#-1}")       # command + flags (including --file-reporter=…)
TARGETS="${!#}"           # final arg: quoted, space-separated target list
[ -n "$TARGETS" ] || usage

CONSOLE="${MAIN_LOG}.console"

# Attempt 1 — the command exactly as the step defines it (its own
# --file-reporter=json:<main-log> is part of CMD; dart accumulates repeated
# reporter flags, so the wrapper must not add a second one).
set +e
"${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS 2>&1 | tee "$CONSOLE"
RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Detection: the ws-drop family signature ONLY — it gates WHETHER this
# wrapper reruns at all. A real assertion failure, compile error, or
# timeout never pairs `Failed to load "…"` with ws text (that prefix is
# emitted solely by the test loader) — with no signature the failure is
# deterministic runner territory: exit here, loud, no rerun.
if ! grep -qE 'Connection closed before full header was received|Connection reset by peer' \
    "$CONSOLE"; then
  echo "load_drop_retry: failure carries no loopback-ws drop signature — not rerunning" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi
DROPPED=$(awk '/Failed to load/ && (/Connection closed before full header was received/ || /Connection reset by peer/)' \
  "$CONSOLE" |
  sed -E -e 's/.*Failed to load "([^"]+)".*/\1/' -e 't' -e 's/.*Failed to load ([^:"]+):.*/\1/' |
  sort -u)
# WHAT to rerun is the FULL attempt-1 failed inventory, not just the
# ws-dropped files (PR #2347 review round 1, blocking): union the console
# drops with every failed suite the attempt-1 reporter recorded
# (gate_failed_targets.py — failure AND error results, load failures via
# the hidden `loading <path>` tests; missing/unparsable log = clean empty).
# A co-occurring real failure is therefore IN the rerun and fails it — the
# shard stays red; an attempt 1 whose ONLY failures are ws drops heals.
REPORTER_FAILED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$MAIN_LOG")
RERUN_TARGETS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$DROPPED" "$REPORTER_FAILED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
if [ -z "$RERUN_TARGETS" ]; then
  echo "load_drop_retry: ws-drop signature present but no failed-file inventory — not rerunning blind" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

echo "🔁 load-drop retry (#2331): rerunning failed file(s) ONCE:" >&2
printf '%s\n' "$RERUN_TARGETS" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2

RETRY_CMD=()
for arg in "${CMD[@]}"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --file-reporter=*) ;;            # rerun writes to RETRY_LOG instead
    *) RETRY_CMD+=("$arg") ;;
  esac
done

set +e
"${RETRY_CMD[@]}" --file-reporter="json:$RETRY_LOG" $RERUN_TARGETS 2>&1 | tee -a "$CONSOLE"
RETRY_RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e

if [ "$RETRY_RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "✅ load-drop retry: healed — dropped file(s) green on the rerun" >&2
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ load-drop retry: rerun still red (exit $RETRY_RC) — failing loudly" >&2
exit "$RETRY_RC"

===
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="build/test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p build/test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2

  fi

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2381 ([ci-red] v1.0.766 failed)

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The v1.0.766 release-gate run (45200064457) went red because PTY/CLI
integration shard 2/3 hung at exit for ~39 minutes, was killed by its
40-minute budget, and the "Advance vpinned marker" job then refused to move
the marker onto an unpublished release; the watchdog retrigger (45208045955)
healed the wedge but red'd a second, independent flake.

**Root cause** (three linked layers, all evidenced from run artifacts):

1. **Trigger — vm-service loopback WS death under load (the issue #2331
   family).** In shard 2/3, after `resume_tail_grid_pty_test.dart` finished
   (t≈32.8 s of `dart test`), the engine's per-suite coverage gather —
   test_core 0.6.21 `engine.dart:301` `await writeCoverage(...)` →
   `RunnerSuite.gatherCoverage()` → `package:coverage` `getSourceReport` —
   failed with `getSourceReport: (-32000) Service connection disposed`.
   The loopback WebSocket between the coverage collector and the VM service
   died mid-run, exactly the load class #2331 documented ("the cap alone
   does not kill the class").
2. **Amplifier — the engine dies BEFORE its queue drains and reports
   success-shaped evidence.** The throw escapes the engine's `FutureGroup`
   task (`package:async future_group.dart:79`), `Runner.run()`'s
   `Future.wait(..., eagerError: true)` rethrows, and `executable.dart`
   prints "This is an unexpected error…" — with the suite queue abandoned:
   the shard's own `--file-reporter` artifact proves it (`allSuites count:
   26` planned, only 16 `suite` events loaded, `testStart: 101` vs
   `testDone: 98`). Three tests were IN FLIGHT when the engine quit
   (`tui_prototype_snapshot_test` "typing text and pressing Enter…",
   `shell_job_countdown_pty_test` "ten background bash jobs…",
   `ssh_shift_gate_test` "SSH session env…") and ~10 suites never loaded.
3. **Wedge — abandoned PTY children block the VM exit handshake (the
   gh-2208/#2122 class).** In-flight tests never reach their `tearDown`s,
   so their pty2 `BlockingPseudoTerminal` children (fa CLIs; the
   `dart run` prototype chain) were still alive at process exit. Each
   pty2 terminal owns a `_waitForExitCode` isolate blocked in native
   `waitpid` (`vendor/pty2/lib/src/impl/unix.dart:455`), which cannot reach
   a safepoint while the child lives → the Dart VM's exit handshake never
   completes → `Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in`
   ×2348 over ~39 minutes → the job-level `timeout-minutes: 40` kill → job
   conclusion `cancelled` (the gh-2290 timeout-kill signature).
4. **Cascade** — `pty-integ-linux = cancelled` → the Quality gate's "fail on
   any real failure" red → the release publish/`Sign release checksums`
   chain never ran → v1.0.766 publishes no `SHA256SUMS` →
   `scripts/pin_release.sh` refuses by design
   (`E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING — the marker must not point at an unsigned
   release`) → "Advance vpinned marker" red → gh-2381 auto-filed.

**The retrigger red (independent)**: run 45208045955 ran shard 2/3 green
(the wedge is load-flaky) but red'd `Hostile ambient env` on
`test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart` AC1 (issue #2260,
line 248): after `entry.stop()`, the settle-side manifest removal runs as an
UNAWAITED IO chain (`_waiting.jobSettled` → `_withRegistryLock` →
tmp+rename write, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_waiting.dart`); the test reads
`running.json` right after `await pumpEventQueue()`, which does not wait for
file-IO completions under load → the assertion observed the pre-removal
manifest (`sh-2260-prev` still listed). Same SHA green in the original run —
a load-timing flake in the test, not a product defect. The identical race
family was fixed for a sibling test in the same release by gh-2378's
bounded observable-effect wait (`waitForManifestId`).

**Impact**: the release train cannot advance the `vpinned` marker past
v1.0.765 until the ref goes green; each wedge burns a 40-minute shard and a
watchdog retrigger; the abandoned-suite hole means a leg can red/green on a
SUBSET of its targets without anyone noticing (10 suites silently absent
from the "passed" shard).

**Fix approach** (minimum, in-repo; the upstream test_core/coverage bugs are
not patchable here):

- A. `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart` AC1: replace the
  `pumpEventQueue()`-then-read with a bounded observable-effect wait
  (the gh-2378 house shape) — observes the settle mutation deterministically,
  fails loudly at the bound.
- B. `scripts/gate_failed_targets.py`: report `--unfinished` (started tests
  with no `testDone` → their suite paths) and `--loaded` (paths from `suite`
  events); the default failed-paths contract stays unchanged.
- C. `scripts/load_drop_retry.sh`: attempt 1 gains an exit-handshake
  watchdog — sustained `waiting for isolate … check in` spam means the run's
  results are already in the file-reporter and coverage is per-suite
  incremental, so the runner is SIGKILLed instead of holding the shard for
  40 minutes — and an abandonment-aware rerun decision: transient targets =
  ws-dropped ∪ unfinished ∪ never-loaded (invocation targets with no suite
  event), rerun ONCE with the full failed union so genuine failures keep the
  shard red (the gh-1026/PR-#2347 discipline, unchanged).

The watchdog retrigger (gh-2290) stays as the outer safety net; this fix
turns the wedge from a 40-minute cancelled burn into a minutes-scoped,
targeted rerun that heals green.

**Previous attempt**: none (first development leg on gh-2381). The gh-2290
watchdog (v1.0.745-era) mitigates the symptom (one retrigger) but does not
address the abandoned-suite evidence or the 40-minute burn.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# load_drop_retry.sh — one-shot retry for sharded dart test legs: the
# loopback-ws load drops (issue #2331) and the engine-abandonment wedge
# (gh-2381).
#
# Family 1 (issue #2331): under CI-leg load the dart test loader's
# loopback WebSocket (127.0.0.1:…/ws) to a freshly spawned test VM can die
# mid-handshake —
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection closed before full header was
#   received, uri = http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection reset by peer, uri=http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
# The victim file is arbitrary (whatever is loading when the socket dies),
# never an assertion failure (6/6 occurrences on the card). The shard reds
# even though every test that ran was green.
#
# Family 2 (gh-2381, run 45200064457 shard 2/3): the same load class can
# kill the VM-service connection DURING a post-suite coverage gather; the
# test_core engine's run loop dies with the suite queue still pending —
# tests left IN FLIGHT (their tearDowns never run → live pty2 children)
# and whole suites never loaded — while the file-reporter records only the
# finished subset (allSuites count 26, 16 suite events, testStart 101 vs
# testDone 98). The abandoned pty2 `_waitForExitCode` isolates then block
# the VM's exit handshake forever (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate
# _waitForExitCode to check in`) and the shard burns its WHOLE budget
# before the timeout kill lands `cancelled`.
#
# This wrapper runs the shard's dart test command as given, and on failure
# that carries a TRANSIENT signature — the ws-drop text above, a started-
# but-never-finished test in the reporter, or an invocation target with no
# suite event at all — re-runs the transient inventory ONCE (the gh-1026
# rerun-only-failed discipline): transient targets PLUS every failed suite
# the attempt-1 reporter records (via the repo's
# scripts/gate_failed_targets.py). A co-occurring real failure — assertion
# failure or compile-error load failure — is therefore IN the rerun and
# keeps the shard red; an attempt 1 whose only losses are transient heals.
# Without a transient signature the wrapper never reruns at all: real
# failures stay loud, nothing is rerun blind, nothing is masked.
#
# The exit-handshake wedge gets a watchdog instead of a 40-minute burn:
# once the console shows sustained `waiting for isolate` spam, the run's
# results are already in the file-reporter (it flushes per event) and
# coverage is per-suite incremental, so the wedged runner is SIGKILLed and
# the normal evidence-driven decision proceeds. The spam budget is
# LOAD_DROP_RETRY_SPAM_LIMIT (default 8 lines; 0 disables the watchdog).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/load_drop_retry.sh <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> "<targets>"
#
#   <main-log>   the path of the caller's own --file-reporter=json:<main-log>
#                (passed as part of <cmd...>) that junit/duration consumers
#                read — attempt-1 evidence is never clobbered; also names
#                the <main-log>.console capture;
#   <retry-log>  where the rerun's reporter writes (kept separate so the
#                main log is never overwritten);
#   <cmd...>     the full dart test invocation INCLUDING its own
#                --file-reporter flag; the FINAL argument is the quoted,
#                newline/space-separated target list (word-split here).
#
# Exit: 0 when the run (or the single rerun) is green; the failing exit
# code otherwise. Coverage consumers are safe: the rerun inherits
# --coverage=coverage, so a healed file's hits land in the same coverage/
# dir the gate merges.
set -euo pipefail
# TARGETS/RERUN_TARGETS expand unquoted below (word-split by design — the
# caller passes a quoted, space-separated list). Glob-off: a path carrying
# glob metacharacters must never expand (PR #2347 review digest).
set -f

usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> \"<targets>\"" >&2
  exit 2
}

[ "$#" -ge 5 ] || usage
MAIN_LOG=$1
RETRY_LOG=$2
[ "${3:-}" = "--" ] || usage
shift 3
CMD=("${@:1:$#-1}")       # command + flags (including --file-reporter=…)
TARGETS="${!#}"           # final arg: quoted, space-separated target list
[ -n "$TARGETS" ] || usage

CONSOLE="${MAIN_LOG}.console"
SPAM_LIMIT="${LOAD_DROP_RETRY_SPAM_LIMIT:-8}"
FIFO=""
WATCHDOG_PID=""

cleanup() {
  [ -n "$WATCHDOG_PID" ] && kill "$WATCHDOG_PID" 2>/dev/null
  rm -f "$FIFO" 2>/dev/null
}
trap cleanup EXIT

# run_streamed <log-target> [--append] — runs CMD+TARGETS with its output
# streamed through <log-target> (`tee`-equivalent evidence) under the
# gh-2381 exit-handshake watchdog; echoes the runner's exit code.
# Single-writer named pipe: the runner's stdout+stderr feed a background
# tee, and `$!` IS the runner pid — an exact kill target with no pgrep
# topology guessing.
run_streamed() {
  local append=false
  [ "${1:-}" = "--append" ] && { append=true; shift; }
  FIFO="${CONSOLE}.fifo"
  mkfifo "$FIFO"
  if $append; then
    tee -a "$CONSOLE" < "$FIFO" &
  else
    tee "$CONSOLE" < "$FIFO" &
  fi
  local tee_pid=$!
  "${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS > "$FIFO" 2>&1 &
  local runner_pid=$!
  if [ "${SPAM_LIMIT:-8}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then (
    while kill -0 "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null; do
      local n
      n=$(grep -c 'waiting for isolate' "$CONSOLE" 2>/dev/null) || n=0
      if [ "${n:-0}" -ge "$SPAM_LIMIT" ]; then
        echo "load_drop_retry: exit-handshake wedge — $n 'waiting for isolate' spam lines; SIGKILL the wedged runner (results are already in the reporter, coverage is per-suite incremental; gh-2381)" >&2
        kill -9 "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null
        break
      fi
      sleep 1
    done
  ) &
    WATCHDOG_PID=$!
  fi
  wait "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null
  local rc=$?
  kill "$WATCHDOG_PID" 2>/dev/null
  WATCHDOG_PID=""
  wait "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$FIFO"
  echo "$rc"
}

# Attempt 1 — the command exactly as the step defines it (its own
# --file-reporter=json:<main-log> is part of CMD; dart accumulates repeated
# reporter flags, so the wrapper must not add a second one).
set +e
RC="$(run_streamed)"
set -e

# Detection: which TRANSIENT family fired, if any. The ws-drop text gates
# family 1; the gh-2381 projections gate family 2 off the SAME reporter
# log. A real assertion failure alone pairs with neither — that shape is
# deterministic runner territory: exit loudly, no rerun.
if ! grep -qE 'Connection closed before full header was received|Connection reset by peer' \
    "$CONSOLE"; then
  DROPPED=""
else
  DROPPED=$(awk '/Failed to load/ && (/Connection closed before full header was received/ || /Connection reset by peer/)' \
    "$CONSOLE" |
    sed -E -e 's/.*Failed to load "([^"]+)".*/\1/' -e 't' -e 's/.*Failed to load ([^:"]+):.*/\1/' |
    sort -u)
fi

# gh-2381 projections: in-flight tests the engine abandoned, and invocation
# targets the engine never even loaded (planned by allSuites, absent from
# the suite events — the ten vanished suites of run 45200064457).
REPORTER_FAILED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$MAIN_LOG")
REPORTER_UNFINISHED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py --unfinished "$MAIN_LOG")
REPORTER_LOADED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py --loaded "$MAIN_LOG")

NEVER_LOADED=""
for t in $TARGETS; do
  if printf '%s\n' "$REPORTER_LOADED" | grep -Fxq -- "$t"; then continue; fi
  if printf '%s\n' "$DROPPED" | grep -Fxq -- "$t"; then continue; fi
  NEVER_LOADED="$NEVER_LOADED$t"$'\n'
done
NEVER_LOADED=$(printf '%s' "$NEVER_LOADED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)

# The transient inventory: every loss this wrapper exists to heal.
TRANSIENT=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$DROPPED" "$REPORTER_UNFINISHED" \
  "$NEVER_LOADED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)

if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && [ -z "$TRANSIENT" ] && [ -z "$REPORTER_FAILED" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

if [ -z "$TRANSIENT" ] && ! grep -qE 'Connection closed before full header was received|Connection reset by peer' \
    "$CONSOLE"; then
  # Real failures only — deterministic, a rerun cannot heal them.
  echo "load_drop_retry: failure carries no transient signature (no loopback-ws drop, no abandoned inventory) — not rerunning" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

# WHAT to rerun is the FULL attempt-1 failed inventory, not just the
# transient files (PR #2347 review round 1, blocking): union the transient
# targets with every failed suite the attempt-1 reporter records. A
# co-occurring real failure is therefore IN the rerun and fails it — the
# shard stays red; an attempt 1 whose ONLY losses are transient heals.
RERUN_TARGETS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$TRANSIENT" "$REPORTER_FAILED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
if [ -z "$RERUN_TARGETS" ]; then
  echo "load_drop_retry: transient signature present but no failed-file inventory — not rerunning blind" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

echo "🔁 load-drop retry (#2331/gh-2381): rerunning transient/failed file(s) ONCE:" >&2
printf '%s\n' "$RERUN_TARGETS" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2

RETRY_CMD=()
for arg in "${CMD[@]}"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --file-reporter=*) ;;            # rerun writes to RETRY_LOG instead
    *) RETRY_CMD+=("$arg") ;;
  esac
done

set +e
CMD=("${RETRY_CMD[@]}")
RC="$(run_streamed --append)"
set -e

if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "✅ load-drop retry: healed — transient loss(es) green on the rerun" >&2
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ load-drop retry: rerun still red (exit $RC) — failing loudly" >&2
exit "$RC"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# load_drop_retry.sh — one-shot retry for sharded dart test legs: the
# loopback-ws load drops (issue #2331) and the engine-abandonment wedge
# (gh-2381).
#
# Family 1 (issue #2331): under CI-leg load the dart test loader's
# loopback WebSocket (127.0.0.1:…/ws) to a freshly spawned test VM can die
# mid-handshake —
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection closed before full header was
#   received, uri = http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection reset by peer, uri=http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
# The victim file is arbitrary (whatever is loading when the socket dies),
# never an assertion failure (6/6 occurrences on the card). The shard reds
# even though every test that ran was green.
#
# Family 2 (gh-2381, run 45200064457 shard 2/3): the same load class can
# kill the VM-service connection DURING a post-suite coverage gather; the
# test_core engine's run loop dies with the suite queue still pending —
# tests left IN FLIGHT (their tearDowns never run → live pty2 children)
# and whole suites never loaded — while the file-reporter records only the
# finished subset (allSuites count 26, 16 suite events, testStart 101 vs
# testDone 98). The abandoned pty2 `_waitForExitCode` isolates then block
# the VM's exit handshake forever (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate
# _waitForExitCode to check in`) and the shard burns its WHOLE budget
# before the timeout kill lands `cancelled`.
#
# This wrapper runs the shard's dart test command as given, and on a run
# carrying a TRANSIENT signature — the ws-drop text above, a started-but-
# never-finished test in the reporter, or an invocation target with no
# suite event at all — re-runs the transient inventory ONCE (the gh-1026
# rerun-only-failed discipline): transient targets PLUS every failed suite
# the attempt-1 reporter records (via the repo's
# scripts/gate_failed_targets.py). A co-occurring real failure — assertion
# failure or compile-error load failure — is therefore IN the rerun and
# keeps the shard red; an attempt 1 whose only losses are transient heals.
# Without a transient signature the wrapper never reruns at all: real
# failures stay loud, nothing is rerun blind, nothing is masked.
#
# The exit-handshake wedge gets a watchdog instead of a 40-minute burn:
# sustained `Attempt:N waiting for isolate …` console spam means the run's
# results are already in the file-reporter (it flushes per event) and
# coverage is per-suite incremental, so the wedged runner is SIGKILLed and
# the normal evidence-driven decision proceeds. The spam budget is
# LOAD_DROP_RETRY_SPAM_LIMIT (default 8 lines; 0 disables the watchdog).
# The pattern is anchored on the `Attempt:` prefix — test-failure text that
# QUOTES the phrase (pty_harness's shutdownPty StateError) never matches.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/load_drop_retry.sh <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> "<targets>"
#
#   <main-log>   the path of the caller's own --file-reporter=json:<main-log>
#                (passed as part of <cmd...>) that junit/duration consumers
#                read — attempt-1 evidence is never clobbered; also names
#                the <main-log>.console capture;
#   <retry-log>  where the rerun's reporter writes (kept separate so the
#                main log is never overwritten);
#   <cmd...>     the full dart test invocation INCLUDING its own
#                --file-reporter flag; the FINAL argument is the quoted,
#                newline/space-separated target list (word-split here).
#
# Exit: 0 when the run (or the single rerun) is green; the failing exit
# code otherwise. Coverage consumers are safe: the rerun inherits
# --coverage=coverage, so a healed file's hits land in the same coverage/
# dir the gate merges.
set -euo pipefail
# TARGETS/RERUN_TARGETS expand unquoted below (word-split by design — the
# caller passes a quoted, space-separated list). Glob-off: a path carrying
# glob metacharacters must never expand (PR #2347 review digest).
set -f

usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> \"<targets>\"" >&2
  exit 2
}

[ "$#" -ge 5 ] || usage
MAIN_LOG=$1
RETRY_LOG=$2
[ "${3:-}" = "--" ] || usage
shift 3
CMD=("${@:1:$#-1}")       # command + flags (including --file-reporter=…)
TARGETS="${!#}"           # final arg: quoted, space-separated target list
[ -n "$TARGETS" ] || usage

CONSOLE="${MAIN_LOG}.console"
SPAM_LIMIT="${LOAD_DROP_RETRY_SPAM_LIMIT:-8}"
FIFO=""
WATCHDOG_PID=""
RUNNER_RC=""

cleanup() {
  if [ -n "$WATCHDOG_PID" ]; then
    kill "$WATCHDOG_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  if [ -n "$FIFO" ]; then
    rm -f "$FIFO" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

# run_streamed [--append] — runs CMD+TARGETS with output streamed to the
# console capture (live CI log) under the gh-2381 exit-handshake watchdog;
# leaves the runner's exit code in RUNNER_RC. Single-writer named pipe: the
# runner's stdout+stderr feed a background tee, and `$!` IS the runner pid
# — an exact kill target with no pgrep topology guessing.
run_streamed() {
  local append=false
  [ "${1:-}" = "--append" ] && append=true
  FIFO="${CONSOLE}.fifo"
  mkfifo "$FIFO"
  if $append; then
    tee -a "$CONSOLE" < "$FIFO" &
  else
    tee "$CONSOLE" < "$FIFO" &
  fi
  local tee_pid=$!
  "${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS > "$FIFO" 2>&1 &
  local runner_pid=$!
  if [ "${SPAM_LIMIT:-8}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    (
      while kill -0 "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null; do
        n=$(grep -cE 'Attempt:[0-9]+ waiting for isolate' "$CONSOLE" 2>/dev/null) || n=0
        if [ "${n:-0}" -ge "$SPAM_LIMIT" ]; then
          echo "load_drop_retry: exit-handshake wedge — $n 'waiting for isolate' spam lines; SIGKILL the wedged runner (results are already in the reporter, coverage is per-suite incremental; gh-2381)" >&2
          kill -9 "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
          break
        fi
        sleep 1
      done
    ) &
    WATCHDOG_PID=$!
  fi
  wait "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null
  RUNNER_RC=$?
  if [ -n "$WATCHDOG_PID" ]; then
    kill "$WATCHDOG_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    WATCHDOG_PID=""
  fi
  wait "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$FIFO" 2>/dev/null || true
  FIFO=""
}

# Attempt 1 — the command exactly as the step defines it (its own
# --file-reporter=json:<main-log> is part of CMD; dart accumulates repeated
# reporter flags, so the wrapper must not add a second one).
set +e
run_streamed
RC=$RUNNER_RC
set -e

# Detection: which TRANSIENT family fired, if any. The ws-drop text gates
# family 1; the gh-2381 projections gate family 2 off the SAME reporter
# log. A real assertion failure alone pairs with neither — that shape is
# deterministic runner territory: exit loudly, no rerun.
if grep -qE 'Connection closed before full header was received|Connection reset by peer' \
    "$CONSOLE"; then
  DROPPED=$(awk '/Failed to load/ && (/Connection closed before full header was received/ || /Connection reset by peer/)' \
    "$CONSOLE" |
    sed -E -e 's/.*Failed to load "([^"]+)".*/\1/' -e 't' -e 's/.*Failed to load ([^:"]+):.*/\1/' |
    sort -u)
else
  DROPPED=""
fi

# gh-2381 projections off the attempt-1 reporter. They are trusted ONLY
# when the log exists and is non-empty — a missing log (crash before the
# reporter flushed) must degrade to the family-1 console evidence alone,
# never to "every target is suspicious" (the no-blind-rerun rule).
REPORTER_FAILED=""
REPORTER_UNFINISHED=""
REPORTER_LOADED=""
HAS_REPORTER=false
if [ -s "$MAIN_LOG" ]; then
  HAS_REPORTER=true
  REPORTER_FAILED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$MAIN_LOG")
  REPORTER_UNFINISHED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py --unfinished "$MAIN_LOG")
  REPORTER_LOADED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py --loaded "$MAIN_LOG")
fi

# Invocation targets the engine never even loaded (planned by allSuites,
# absent from the suite events — the ten vanished suites of run 45200064457).
NEVER_LOADED=""
if $HAS_REPORTER; then
  for t in $TARGETS; do
    if printf '%s\n' "$REPORTER_LOADED" | grep -Fxq -- "$t"; then continue; fi
    if printf '%s\n' "$DROPPED" | grep -Fxq -- "$t"; then continue; fi
    NEVER_LOADED="$NEVER_LOADED$t"$'\n'
  done
  NEVER_LOADED=$(printf '%s' "$NEVER_LOADED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
fi

# The transient inventory: every loss this wrapper exists to heal.
TRANSIENT=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$DROPPED" "$REPORTER_UNFINISHED" \
  "$NEVER_LOADED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)

if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && [ -z "$TRANSIENT" ] && [ -z "$REPORTER_FAILED" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

if [ -z "$TRANSIENT" ]; then
  # Real failures only — deterministic, a rerun cannot heal them.
  echo "load_drop_retry: failure carries no transient signature (no loopback-ws drop, no abandoned inventory) — not rerunning" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

# WHAT to rerun is the FULL attempt-1 failed inventory, not just the
# transient files (PR #2347 review round 1, blocking): union the transient
# targets with every failed suite the attempt-1 reporter records. A
# co-occurring real failure is therefore IN the rerun and fails it — the
# shard stays red; an attempt 1 whose ONLY losses are transient heals.
RERUN_TARGETS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$TRANSIENT" "$REPORTER_FAILED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
if [ -z "$RERUN_TARGETS" ]; then
  echo "load_drop_retry: transient signature present but no failed-file inventory — not rerunning blind" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

echo "🔁 load-drop retry (#2331/gh-2381): rerunning transient/failed file(s) ONCE:" >&2
printf '%s\n' "$RERUN_TARGETS" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2

RETRY_CMD=()
for arg in "${CMD[@]}"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --file-reporter=*) ;;            # rerun writes to RETRY_LOG instead
    *) RETRY_CMD+=("$arg") ;;
  esac
done

set +e
CMD=("${RETRY_CMD[@]}")
run_streamed --append
RC=$RUNNER_RC
set -e

if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "✅ load-drop retry: healed — transient loss(es) green on the rerun" >&2
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ load-drop retry: rerun still red (exit $RC) — failing loudly" >&2
exit "$RC"

content.text:
RC=$RUNNER_RC
set -e

# Detection: which TRANSIENT family fired, if any. The ws-drop text gates
# family 1; the gh-2381 projections gate family 2 off the SAME reporter
# log. A real assertion failure alone pairs with neither — that shape is
# deterministic runner territory: exit loudly, no rerun.
if grep -qE 'Connection closed before full header was received|Connection reset by peer' \
    "$CONSOLE"; then
  DROPPED=$(awk '/Failed to load/ && (/Connection closed before full header was received/ || /Connection reset by peer/)' \
    "$CONSOLE" |
    sed -E -e 's/.*Failed to load "([^"]+)".*/\1/' -e 't' -e 's/.*Failed to load ([^:"]+):.*/\1/' |
    sort -u)
else
  DROPPED=""
fi

# gh-2381 projections off the attempt-1 reporter. They are trusted ONLY
# when the log exists and is non-empty — a missing log (crash before the
# reporter flushed) must degrade to the family-1 console evidence alone,
# never to "every target is suspicious" (the no-blind-rerun rule).
REPORTER_FAILED=""
REPORTER_UNFINISHED=""
REPORTER_LOADED=""
HAS_REPORTER=false
if [ -s "$MAIN_LOG" ]; then
  HAS_REPORTER=true
  REPORTER_FAILED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$MAIN_LOG")
  REPORTER_UNFINISHED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py --unfinished "$MAIN_LOG")
  REPORTER_LOADED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py --loaded "$MAIN_LOG")
fi

# Invocation targets the engine never even loaded (planned by allSuites,
# absent from the suite events — the ten vanished suites of run 45200064457).
NEVER_LOADED=""
if $HAS_REPORTER; then
  for t in $TARGETS; do
    if printf '%s\n' "$REPORTER_LOADED" | grep -Fxq -- "$t"; then continue; fi
    if printf '%s\n' "$DROPPED" | grep -Fxq -- "$t"; then continue; fi
    NEVER_LOADED="$NEVER_LOADED$t"$'\n'
  done
  NEVER_LOADED=$(printf '%s' "$NEVER_LOADED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
fi

# The transient inventory: every loss this wrapper exists to heal.
TRANSIENT=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$DROPPED" "$REPORTER_UNFINISHED" \
  "$NEVER_LOADED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)

if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && [ -z "$TRANSIENT" ] && [ -z "$REPORTER_FAILED" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

if [ -z "$TRANSIENT" ]; then
  # Real failures only — deterministic, a rerun cannot heal them.
  echo "load_drop_retry: failure carries no transient signature (no loopback-ws drop, no abandoned inventory) — not rerunning" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

# WHAT to rerun is the FULL attempt-1 failed inventory, not just the
# transient files (PR #2347 review round 1, blocking): union the transient
# targets with every failed suite the attempt-1 reporter records. A
# co-occurring real failure is therefore IN the rerun and fails it — the
# shard stays red; an attempt 1 whose ONLY losses are transient heals.
RERUN_TARGETS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$TRANSIENT" "$REPORTER_FAILED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
if [ -z "$RERUN_TARGETS" ]; then
  echo "load_drop_retry: transient signature present but no failed-file inventory — not rerunning blind" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

echo "🔁 load-drop retry (#2331/gh-2381): rerunning transient/failed file(s) ONCE:" >&2
printf '%s\n' "$RERUN_TARGETS" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2

RETRY_CMD=()
for arg in "${CMD[@]}"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --file-reporter=*) ;;            # rerun writes to RETRY_LOG instead
    *) RETRY_CMD+=("$arg") ;;
  esac
done
