The redirect `>"$FIFO"` is performed BY THE SUBSHELL CHILD, not the parent ✓. Hmm — but wait: bash optimizes simple commands with only a redirect... no fork? A background command ALWAYS forks ✓. So the child holds the fd; SIGKILL closes it.

BUT — the RUNER here is `bash /tmp/wedgedbg/stub.sh` — bash exec's the script? The child bash opens the fifo, then runs the stub — the stub spawns `sleep 300` as ITS child — `sleep` INHERITS the fifo write-end fd!! `kill -9 runner_pid` kills the stub bash, but **sleep 300 keeps the fifo write-end open** → tee never EOFs → `wait tee_pid` blocks... wait — do I wait on tee BEFORE returning? `wait "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || true` — yes!! THAT's the hang: tee waits for ALL writers to close (sleep holds it). The wrapper waits for tee → blocked → timeout.

In the REAL CI case: dart test (the runner) spawns CHILDREN (the AOT fa processes over pty2, flutter test subprocesses...) — all inherit the fifo write-end fd → killing dart test would NOT close the fifo → tee hangs → the wrapper hangs → THE EXACT SAME BUG. (In CI the dart children get reparented — still holding the fifo.)

FIXES:
(a) `CLOEXEC`-like behavior: open the fifo fd in the SHELL, mark close-on-exec, and pass it via fd redirection: 
``
exec {fifo_fd}> "$FIFO"  # shell opens; bash sets CLOEXEC on {var}> fds!
"${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS >&"$fifo_fd" 2>&1 &
runner_pid=$!
``
Bash's `{var}>file` redirections are opened by the SHELL with FD_CLOEXEC set — child processes do NOT inherit them; the child's stdout is dup'd from the shell's fd AT FORK TIME — hmm wait — if the fd is CLOEXEC, the redirection `>&$fd` in the child... The redirection happens in the forked child BEFORE exec: the child dups fd N onto 1 — the DUP survives exec (dups of a CLOEXEC fd are NOT cloexec — the flag lives on the fd description... actually dup2 clears cloexec on the NEW fd ✓). So: child's stdout = a dup of the fifo fd, NOT cloexec... the child then execs dart — stdout stays connected. Dart spawns children — THEY inherit stdout (the fifo dup) — same leak!! The dup'd fd doesn't have cloexec.

Hmm — so (a) doesn't fix grandchild inheritance.

(b) The REAL semantics needed: the wrapper should stop waiting for the stream once the RUNER is dead. When the runner dies (killed or normal), remaining writers (its children) are irrelevant — evidence is complete. So: DON'T wait for tee at all! After `wait $runner_pid`, leave tee running in the background?? It'll hold... the fifo write-ends held by orphans keep tee alive FOREVER (until the orphan dies — sleep 300 → tee exits in ≤300s; dart's pty children die at job end). Leaking tee for the job duration = harmless-ish but sloppy; orphaned tee + CONSOLE final state — evidence already complete (results recorded before the wedge).

Hmm — but `set -euo pipefail` + the script exiting while a background tee runs → bash exits, tee orphaned → CI marks "orphan processes"... The finalize cleanup kills them (the v1.0.766 log showed Actions' orphan cleanup!). Not ideal but acceptable? Better:

(c) KILL the runner's process GROUP: launch the runner in its own process group (`setsid` or `set -m`) and `kill -9 -$group` — kills dart AND ALL its children (sleep 300, fa, tee-inheritance gone — all dead → fifo closes → tee EOFs → wrapper returns). This is EXACTLY right for the wedge: the abandoned pty children of dart test MUST die anyway (they're the wedge source!). CI runners have setsid ✓ (the repo's own tests require setsid).

With setsid: `setsid bash stub.sh ... > fifo 2>&1 &` — setsid makes the runner a session/group leader (pgid = its pid). Kill: `kill -9 -$runner_pid` (negative = the group). Children inherit the group → all die ✓. Then tee EOFs ✓. Then wait runner → 137 ✓. `wait tee` → returns ✓. CLEAN.

setsid availability: util-linux — on ubuntu runners ✓ (repo tests already require it). Fallback: if setsid is missing → launch without it and skip group-kill (kill only the runner; tee may linger — degrade gracefully via a bounded tee wait).

Implementation:
``
if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 setsid "${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS > "$FIFO" 2>&1 &
else
 "${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS > "$FIFO" 2>&1 &
fi
runner_pid=$!
...
kill -9 "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null
kill -9 -- "-$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true  # the group (setsid mode)
``
Note: `kill -9 -- -PID` when NOT a group leader (no setsid) would fail (ESRCH or kill OTHER processes?!) — killing "-runner_pid" when runner_pid is NOT a pgid: kill(-pid) targets the process GROUP with that id — if no such group → ESRCH error → || true. DANGER: if pid reuse made some OTHER group with that id... vanishingly rare in the 2-second window; accept.

And normal exit path: the runner exits by itself; its children (fa CLIs already reaped by the test's tearDowns) — in a NORMAL dart test run, does dart test leave children at exit? The CI evidence: after the ORIGINAL (non-wedged) 14-file run, the orphan cleanup found bash/dart:concatenat/tee/dartdev_ao — YES dart test leaves grandchildren (the tui orphan etc.) — with setsid those are in the runner's group but the runner EXITED by itself — we don't group-kill on the normal path (only on the watchdog path) → tee lingers while orphans hold the fifo... SAME LEAK on the normal path!! The normal path: runner exits naturally → tee STILL blocked until all writer fds close (orphans hold the fifo write-end for the job's duration) → wait tee_pid BLOCKS → wrapper hangs on EVERY NORMAL RUN. FATAL.

So I MUST handle tee's lifetime independent of writers:
- Option A: `tee ... < "$FIFO" &` + after the runner exits (normal or killed), kill tee: tee dies; leftover fifo WRITERS (orphans) then get SIGPIPE on their next write → fine (they're orphans anyway). `wait tee_pid` returns after the kill ✓. Evidence complete (the runner's output all drained? — if the runner exited normally, its output was fully written; tee may have buffered a few bytes — kill after a brief drain? Practically: runner exit → its writes are in the pipe/fifo buffer → tee consumes fast → kill tee AFTER `wait runner` + a tiny drain `sleep 0.1`? A cleaner drain: wait for tee to EOF on its own OR a short deadline:
 ```
 drained=false
 for in 1 2 3 4 5; do
   if ! kill -0 "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null; then drained=true; break; fi
   read -t 0.2 -u 3 || true  # 0.2s builtin timer
 done
 kill "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
 ```
 read -t 0.2 — fractional seconds supported in bash ≥4 ✓ (ubuntu bash 5.x). 

 On the WEDGE path: same drain loop (tee already EOFed since group-kill closed all writer fds) → drained quickly ✓.
 On the NORMAL path: tee lingers (orphan-held writers) → after 5×0.2s we kill tee → wrapper returns ✓. The remaining orphan writers get EPIPE/SIGPIPE on next write (dart's orphan tui writes to ITS pty, not our fifo — only direct stdio holders matter — they hold the DUP of the fifo; on exit nothing breaks).

 Evidence integrity on the normal path: all runner output written BEFORE runner exit; the fifo kernel buffer + tee consumed it — 1s drain is plenty. The rerun's --append gets its evidence ✓. The junit/duration consumers read the reporter json, not the console ✓.

- Combine with setsid group-kill on the wedge path (so grandchildren die — semantically RIGHT: the wedge's whole point is abandoned children must die; leaving them alive would ALSO leave the test process tree burning CPU — e.g. countdown's 10 sleep jobs — during the rerun!). YES — group-kill is required.

So final design:
- runner launched via setsid (fallback plain).
- watchdog: on spam → `kill -9 -- -$runner_pid` (group; falls back to plain pid kill).
- after `wait runner_pid`: drain loop (≤1s) → kill tee → wait tee.

Note the watchdog message + the group-kill ordering: kill group FIRST then plain pid.

One more subtlety — `setsid` + `$!`: setsid execs the command directly (setsid fork-execs; $! = setsid's pid = the new session leader's pid IF setsid doesn't fork. `setsid cmd` when the calling shell's child... setsid forks if it's already a group leader (rare in scripts) — mostly it execs directly → $! IS the runner pid AND the group leader ✓. If setsid DID fork (rare), runner_pid = setsid's pid which exited instantly → wait returns immediately → wrong. Guard: after launching, verify the process exists... keep simple: `setsid --wait`?? --wait makes setsid wait for the child — then $! = setsid which stays alive ✓ and signals to setsid's pid... `kill -TERM setsid_pid` doesn't propagate to the child! Ugh. Use plain `setsid cmd &` and handle the rare fork case: setsid forks only when it IS already a process-group leader — a freshly backgrounded child is NOT the leader (its pgid = the script's group, and it's not the leader unless pid==pgid coincidence... actually a new child HAS pid==its own; pgid inherited = script's pgid ≠ child pid → not leader → setsid execs directly ✓). Safe.

Let me rewrite run_streamed accordingly.

content.text: The hang: killed runner's GRANDCHILDREN (the stub's `sleep 300` — in CI, dart's spawned processes) inherit the fifo write-end, so `tee` never EOFs. Fix: launch the runner via `setsid` (own process group → group-kill on the wedge path kills the whole tree) and stop waiting on `tee` — drain briefly, then kill it:

arguments.newText:
# run_streamed [--append] — runs CMD+TARGETS with output streamed to the
# console capture (live CI log) under the gh-2381 exit-handshake watchdog;
# leaves the runner's exit code in RUNNER_RC. Single-writer named pipe: the
# runner's stdout+stderr feed a background tee, and `$!` IS the runner pid
# — an exact kill target with no pgrep topology guessing.
#
# The runner rides `setsid` (own process group) so the watchdog's wedge
# kill takes the WHOLE tree down: a killed dart test leaves its spawned
# children (pty CLIs, `dart run` chains, sleeps) holding the fifo's write
# end — without the group kill, `tee` never sees EOF and this wrapper
# hangs exactly like the wedge it is killing. After the runner exits, tee
# gets a short drain window (an orphan-held write end can keep it alive
# forever) and is then killed; the evidence is complete the moment the
# runner's writes land.
run_streamed() {
  local append=false
  [ "${1:-}" = "--append" ] && append=true
  FIFO="${CONSOLE}.fifo"
  mkfifo "$FIFO"
  if $append; then
    tee -a "$CONSOLE" < "$FIFO" &
  else
    tee "$CONSOLE" < "$FIFO" &
  fi
  local tee_pid=$!
  if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    setsid "${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS > "$FIFO" 2>&1 &
  else
    "${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS > "$FIFO" 2>&1 &
  fi
  local runner_pid=$!
  if [ "${SPAM_LIMIT:-8}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    (
      # `read -t 1` is the poll timer: a BUILTIN — killing this subshell
      # mid-wait forks no `sleep` child for the job harness to report.
      exec 3< /dev/zero
      while kill -0 "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null; do
        n=$(grep -cE 'Attempt:[0-9]+ waiting for isolate' "$CONSOLE" 2>/dev/null) || n=0
        if [ "${n:-0}" -ge "$SPAM_LIMIT" ]; then
          echo "load_drop_retry: exit-handshake wedge — $n 'waiting for isolate' spam lines; SIGKILL the wedged runner's process group (results are already in the reporter, coverage is per-suite incremental; gh-2381)" >&2
          kill -9 -- "-$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
          kill -9 "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
          break
        fi
        read -t 1 -u 3 || true
      done
    ) &
    WATCHDOG_PID=$!
  fi
  wait "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null
  RUNNER_RC=$?
  if [ -n "$WATCHDOG_PID" ]; then
    kill "$WATCHDOG_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    WATCHDOG_PID=""
  fi
  # Drain window: on the wedge path the group kill closed every write end
  # and tee EOFs on its own; on the normal path orphan-held writers can
  # keep tee alive indefinitely — cap the drain and kill it.
  exec 3< /dev/zero
  local i
  for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
    kill -0 "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    read -t 0.2 -u 3 || true
  done
  kill "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$FIFO" 2>/dev/null || true
  FIFO=""
}

228:  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."

256:    dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
259:    "test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart"
294:      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
305:        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
481:    test-core) stage_test_core ;;
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  # Issue #2227: the trio rides NO quarantine filter (gh-1033: the CLI
  # coverage ratchet needs these hits pre-merge), so the #2331 loopback-ws
  # load-drop family reaches this leg unhealed — a dropped loader ws reds
  # the gate on an arbitrary victim file while every test that ran was
  # green. Same one-shot wrapper as the sharded legs: a dropped file
  # reruns ONCE (the rerun inherits --coverage=coverage — healed hits land
  # in the same coverage/ dir format_coverage merges); real failures carry
  # no ws-drop signature and stay loud. Keep the target list in sync with
  # ci.yml (test-core shard 0).
  mkdir -p build/test-results
  bash scripts/load_drop_retry.sh \
    "build/test-results/cli-trio-lcov.json" \

    --coverage=coverage \
    --file-reporter="json:build/test-results/cli-trio-lcov.json" \
    "test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart"

### Root Cause
- v1.0.766's PTY shard 2/3 died from a three-layer chain: the vm-service loopback WS died mid-coverage-gather (the #2331 load class); the test_core engine's run loop threw with its queue still pending (3 tests in flight, 10 suites never loaded — proven by the shard's own reporter: allSuites 26, 16 suite events, testStart 101 vs testDone 98); the abandoned suites' live pty2 children blocked the VM exit handshake (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode`, ×2348) until the 40-minute kill concluded the job `cancelled` → Quality gate red → no signed SHA256SUMS → `pin_release.sh` refused (`E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING`) → "Advance vpinned marker" red.
- The watchdog retrigger healed the wedge but red'd `Hostile ambient env`: `agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart` AC1 (#2260) reads `running.json` right after `pumpEventQueue()`, but the settle-side manifest removal is an unawaited file-IO chain — under load the assertion observed the pre-removal manifest (same SHA green in the original run).

### Fix
- `scripts/load_drop_retry.sh`: the sharded legs' wrapper now SIGKILLs a wedged runner on sustained `Attempt:N waiting for isolate` console spam (results are already in the file-reporter; coverage is per-suite incremental) instead of burning the shard budget, and heals the abandonment: reruns unfinished-test suites + never-loaded invocation targets ONCE, same rerun-only-transient discipline — real failures join the rerun and keep the shard red; a missing reporter never reruns blind.
- `scripts/gate_failed_targets.py`: `--unfinished` (started tests with no `testDone` → their suite paths) and `--loaded` (suite-event paths) projections; the default failed-paths contract for `FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES` is unchanged (verified: run 45200064457's real shard artifact → `--unfinished` = the 3 in-flight suites, `--loaded` = 16).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart` AC1: the manifest leave is now observed via a bounded load-tolerant wait (gh-2378 house shape) with a loud fail at the bound.

### Test Coverage
- `test/scripts/gate_failed_targets_test.dart`: 15 tests — unfinished/loaded projections incl. a fixture of the REAL abandonment log.
- `test/scripts/load_drop_retry_test.dart`: 13 tests — AC10-13 drive the real wrapper with stubbed runners: wedge spam → kill → exact abandoned-inventory rerun → heals; rerun-still-red stays loud; exit-70 unfinished and never-loaded-only (exit 0!) both rerun.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart`: 29 tests pass.
- Full `dart test --exclude-tags integration,browser-ext,llm` suite: green (see final numbers below).

### Notes
- No product-code changes — CI infra + one flaky test; the wrapper's fast path (green run, no transient signature) exits 0 with a single invocation, byte-identical behavior to before.
- The gh-2290 watchdog retrigger stays as the outer net; this fix turns the wedge class from a cancelled 40-minute burn into a minutes-scoped targeted rerun.

WATCHDOG_PID=""
RUNNER_RC=""

cleanup() {
  if [ -n "$WATCHDOG_PID" ]; then
    kill "$WATCHDOG_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  if [ -n "$FIFO" ]; then
    rm -f "$FIFO" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

# run_streamed [--append] — runs CMD+TARGETS with output streamed to the
# console capture (live CI log) under the gh-2381 exit-handshake watchdog;
# leaves the runner's exit code in RUNNER_RC. Single-writer named pipe: the
# runner's stdout+stderr feed a background tee, and `$!` IS the runner pid
# — an exact kill target with no pgrep topology guessing.
#
# The runner rides `setsid` (own process group) so the watchdog's wedge
# kill takes the WHOLE tree down: a killed dart test leaves its spawned
# children (pty CLIs, `dart run` chains, sleeps) holding the fifo's write
# end — without the group kill, `tee` never sees EOF and this wrapper
# hangs exactly like the wedge it is killing. After the runner exits, tee
# gets a short drain window (an orphan-held write end can keep it alive
# forever) and is then killed; the evidence is complete the moment the
# runner's writes land.
run_streamed() {
  local append=false
  [ "${1:-}" = "--append" ] && append=true
  FIFO="${CONSOLE}.fifo"
  mkfifo "$FIFO"
  if $append; then
    tee -a "$CONSOLE" < "$FIFO" &
  else
    tee "$CONSOLE" < "$FIFO" &
  fi
  local tee_pid=$!
  if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    setsid "${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS > "$FIFO" 2>&1 &
  else
    "${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS > "$FIFO" 2>&1 &
  fi
  local runner_pid=$!
  if [ "${SPAM_LIMIT:-8}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    (
      # `read -t 1` is the poll timer: a BUILTIN — killing this subshell
      # mid-wait forks no `sleep` child for the job harness to report.
      exec 3< /dev/zero
      while kill -0 "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null; do
        n=$(grep -cE 'Attempt:[0-9]+ waiting for isolate' "$CONSOLE" 2>/dev/null) || n=0
        if [ "${n:-0}" -ge "$SPAM_LIMIT" ]; then
          echo "load_drop_retry: exit-handshake wedge — $n 'waiting for isolate' spam lines; SIGKILL the wedged runner's process group (results are already in the reporter, coverage is per-suite incremental; gh-2381)" >&2
          kill -9 -- "-$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
          kill -9 "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
          break
        fi
        read -t 1 -u 3 || true
      done
    ) &
    WATCHDOG_PID=$!
  fi
  wait "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null
  RUNNER_RC=$?
  if [ -n "$WATCHDOG_PID" ]; then
    kill "$WATCHDOG_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    WATCHDOG_PID=""
  fi
  # Drain window: on the wedge path the group kill closed every write end
  # and tee EOFs on its own; on the normal path orphan-held writers can
  # keep tee alive indefinitely — cap the drain and kill it.
  exec 3< /dev/zero
  local i
  for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
    kill -0 "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    read -t 0.2 -u 3 || true
  done
  kill "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$FIFO" 2>/dev/null || true
  FIFO=""
}

# Attempt 1 — the command exactly as the step defines it (its own
# --file-reporter=json:<main-log> is part of CMD; dart accumulates repeated
# reporter flags, so the wrapper must not add a second one).
set +e
run_streamed
RC=$RUNNER_RC
set -e

# Detection: which TRANSIENT family fired, if any. The ws-drop text gates
# family 1; the gh-2381 projections gate family 2 off the SAME reporter
# log. A real assertion failure alone pairs with neither — that shape is
# deterministic runner territory: exit loudly, no rerun.
if grep -qE 'Connection closed before full header was received|Connection reset by peer' \
    "$CONSOLE"; then
  DROPPED=$(awk '/Failed to load/ && (/Connection closed before full header was received/ || /Connection reset by peer/)' \
    "$CONSOLE" |
    sed -E -e 's/.*Failed to load "([^"]+)".*/\1/' -e 't' -e 's/.*Failed to load ([^:"]+):.*/\1/' |
    sort -u)
else
  DROPPED=""
fi

# gh-2381 projections off the attempt-1 reporter. They are trusted ONLY
# when the log exists and is non-empty — a missing log (crash before the
# reporter flushed) must degrade to the family-1 console evidence alone,
# never to "every target is suspicious" (the no-blind-rerun rule).
REPORTER_FAILED=""
REPORTER_UNFINISHED=""
REPORTER_LOADED=""
HAS_REPORTER=false
if [ -s "$MAIN_LOG" ]; then
  HAS_REPORTER=true
  REPORTER_FAILED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$MAIN_LOG")
  REPORTER_UNFINISHED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py --unfinished "$MAIN_LOG")
  REPORTER_LOADED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py --loaded "$MAIN_LOG")
fi

# Invocation targets the engine never even loaded (planned by allSuites,
# absent from the suite events — the ten vanished suites of run 45200064457).
NEVER_LOADED=""
if $HAS_REPORTER; then
  for t in $TARGETS; do
    if printf '%s\n' "$REPORTER_LOADED" | grep -Fxq -- "$t"; then continue; fi
    if printf '%s\n' "$DROPPED" | grep -Fxq -- "$t"; then continue; fi
    NEVER_LOADED="$NEVER_LOADED$t"$'\n'
  done
  NEVER_LOADED=$(printf '%s' "$NEVER_LOADED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
fi

# The transient inventory: every loss this wrapper exists to heal.
TRANSIENT=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$DROPPED" "$REPORTER_UNFINISHED" \
  "$NEVER_LOADED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)

if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && [ -z "$TRANSIENT" ] && [ -z "$REPORTER_FAILED" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

if [ -z "$TRANSIENT" ]; then
  # Real failures only — deterministic, a rerun cannot heal them.
  echo "load_drop_retry: failure carries no transient signature (no loopback-ws drop, no abandoned inventory) — not rerunning" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

# WHAT to rerun is the FULL attempt-1 failed inventory, not just the
# transient files (PR #2347 review round 1, blocking): union the transient
# targets with every failed suite the attempt-1 reporter records. A
# co-occurring real failure is therefore IN the rerun and fails it — the
# shard stays red; an attempt 1 whose ONLY losses are transient heals.
RERUN_TARGETS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$TRANSIENT" "$REPORTER_FAILED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
if [ -z "$RERUN_TARGETS" ]; then
  echo "load_drop_retry: transient signature present but no failed-file inventory — not rerunning blind" >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

echo "🔁 load-drop retry (#2331/gh-2381): rerunning transient/failed file(s) ONCE:" >&2
printf '%s\n' "$RERUN_TARGETS" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2

RETRY_CMD=()
for arg in "${CMD[@]}"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --file-reporter=*) ;;            # rerun writes to RETRY_LOG instead
    *) RETRY_CMD+=("$arg") ;;
  esac
done
RETRY_CMD+=("--file-reporter=json:$RETRY_LOG")

set +e
CMD=("${RETRY_CMD[@]}")
TARGETS="$RERUN_TARGETS"   # the rerun drives the transient/failed inventory
run_streamed --append
RC=$RUNNER_RC
set -e

if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "✅ load-drop retry: healed — transient loss(es) green on the rerun" >&2
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ load-drop retry: rerun still red (exit $RC) — failing loudly" >&2
exit "$RC"

## Development Mode: Plan (plan-mode protocol appendix)

This leg runs in **plan mode**: work through an explicit, committed task
plan instead of free-form execution. Everything else in the instruction
pack still applies unchanged — this appendix only structures HOW you work.
`<KEY>` below is the current ticket key.

### 1. Decompose before editing

- Before writing any production code, break the ticket into numbered tasks
  `T1..Tn` in `outputs/<KEY>/plan.md` (the working copy).
- Every task carries exactly two fields:
  - `what` — the concrete change this task makes;
  - `verify` — how to check it passed (the command to run and the expected
    result).
- End the plan with two sections:
  - `## Decisions` — the chosen approach for every open point;
  - `## Open questions` — anything unresolved, with the workaround you picked.

### 2. Mirror the plan into a committed snapshot

- Mirror the plan to `.dmtools/plan-snapshot.md` and commit it on the dev
  branch right away: commit subject `<KEY>: plan`.

  interruption windows and CI session-cache loss. (`outputs/` never rides
  commits.)
- When a task completes: mark its checkbox `[x]` in BOTH files and commit
  the snapshot update: `<KEY>: plan update T# done` (one commit per task).
- The periodic WIP auto-save commits keep running as usual; your plan
  commits coexist with them.

### 3. Resume rule (continuation legs)

- At leg start: if a plan file (`outputs/<KEY>/plan.md` or
  `.dmtools/plan-snapshot.md`) already exists, or the branch already carries
  commits, this leg is a CONTINUATION, not a fresh start:
  1. Read the plan and `git log`.
  2. Reconcile the plan checkboxes against the actual branch diff — a task
     whose change is already on the branch is done, checkbox or not.
  3. Execute ONLY the still-pending tasks.

### 4. Close out — the plan file never rides the pull request

- When the LAST task is done (every checkbox `[x]`), remove the snapshot
  from the branch again: `git rm .dmtools/plan-snapshot.md`, commit
  subject `<KEY>: plan done`.
- Do this BEFORE writing `outputs/<KEY>/response.md`: the completion
  report is the leg's deliverable — the plan file is leg scaffolding.
- The engine repeats this cleanup defensively before the PR is created,
  so an open pull request never carries the plan file.

python3 - << 'EOF'
p = 'test/scripts/load_drop_retry_test.dart'
s = open(p).read()
old = """  wedge-abandon|wedge-abandon-rerun-red)
    echo '$droppedClosedHeader'
    exit 1 ;;
"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
new = """  wedge-abandon|wedge-abandon-rerun-red)
    echo '$droppedClosedHeader'
    exit 1 ;;
  wedge-slow-rerun)
    # AC14: the rerun writes its retry reporter BEFORE exiting — a slow
    # enough start that a stale-spam watchdog poll would land mid-run.
    if [ -f "$tmp/attempt2" ]; then
      printf '%s\\n' '{"type":"done","success":true}' > "\\$main"
      sleep 2
      exit 0
    fi
    touch "$tmp/attempt2"
    printf '%s\\n' '{"type":"suite","suite":{"id":1,"path":"test/healthy_test.dart","platform":"vm"}}' > "\\$main"
    printf '%s\\n' '{"type":"testStart","test":{"id":10,"name":"healthy case","suiteID":1,"groupIDs":[]},"time":0}' >> "\\$main"
    printf '%s\\n' '{"type":"testDone","testID":10,"result":"success","hidden":false,"skipped":false,"time":5}' >> "\\$main"
    printf '%s\\n' '{"type":"done","success":true}' >> "\\$main"
    echo 'Attempt:1 waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in'
    echo 'Attempt:2 waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in'
    echo 'Attempt:3 waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in'
    sleep 300
    exit 0 ;;
"""
open(p, 'w').write(s.replace(old, new))
print("wedge-slow-rerun mode added")
EOF

content.text:
usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> \"<targets>\"" >&2
  exit 2
}

[ "$#" -ge 5 ] || usage
MAIN_LOG=$1
RETRY_LOG=$2
[ "${3:-}" = "--" ] || usage
shift 3
CMD=("${@:1:$#-1}")       # command + flags (including --file-reporter=…)
TARGETS="${!#}"           # final arg: quoted, space-separated target list
[ -n "$TARGETS" ] || usage

CONSOLE="${MAIN_LOG}.console"
BACKOFF=${LOAD_DROP_RETRY_BACKOFF_S:-5}
MAX_RERUNS=${LOAD_DROP_RETRY_MAX_RERUNS:-2}
# Operator knobs are consumed by bash integer tests/arithmetic below. A
# sleep-style "5s" or other garbage must not disable the retry loop itself.
[[ "$BACKOFF" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || BACKOFF=5
[[ "$MAX_RERUNS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || MAX_RERUNS=2

# Attempt 1 — the command exactly as the step defines it (its own
# --file-reporter=json:<main-log> is part of CMD; dart accumulates repeated
# reporter flags, so the wrapper must not add a second one).
set +e
"${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS 2>&1 | tee "$CONSOLE"
RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e

RERUNS=0
SEGMENT="$CONSOLE"     # the FAILING attempt's own output (detection input)
REPORTER="$MAIN_LOG"   # that attempt's reporter log (rerun inventory input)

while [ "$RC" -ne 0 ] && [ "$RERUNS" -lt "$MAX_RERUNS" ]; do
  # Detection gates WHETHER this wrapper reruns at all: the ws-drop family
  # signature on the FAILING attempt's own segment — a healed attempt-1
  # line living in the accumulated console can never re-arm the loop. A
  # real assertion failure, compile error, or timeout never pairs
  # `Failed to load "…"` with ws text (that prefix is emitted solely by
  # the test loader) — with no signature the failure is deterministic
  # runner territory: exit here, loud, no rerun.
  if ! grep -qE 'Connection closed before full header was received|Connection reset by peer' \
    "$SEGMENT"; then
    echo "load_drop_retry: failure carries no loopback-ws drop signature — not rerunning" >&2
    exit "$RC"
  fi
  DROPPED=$(awk '/Failed to load/ && (/Connection closed before full header was received/ || /Connection reset by peer/)' \
    "$SEGMENT" |
    sed -E -e 's/.*Failed to load "([^"]+)".*/\1/' -e 't' -e 's/.*Failed to load ([^:"]+):.*/\1/' |
    sort -u)
  # WHAT to rerun is the FULL failed inventory of the failing attempt, not
  # just the ws-dropped files (PR #2347 review round 1, blocking): union
  # the console drops with every failed suite the attempt's reporter
  # recorded (gate_failed_targets.py — failure AND error results, load
  # failures via the hidden `loading <path>` tests; missing/unparsable log
  # = clean empty). A co-occurring real failure is therefore IN the rerun
  # and fails it — the shard stays red; an attempt whose ONLY failures are
  # ws drops heals.
  REPORTER_FAILED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$REPORTER")
  RERUN_TARGETS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$DROPPED" "$REPORTER_FAILED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
  if [ -z "$RERUN_TARGETS" ]; then
    echo "load_drop_retry: ws-drop signature present but no failed-file inventory — not rerunning blind" >&2
    exit "$RC"
  fi

  RERUNS=$((RERUNS + 1))
  echo "🔁 load-drop retry (#2331): rerun $RERUNS/$MAX_RERUNS after ${BACKOFF}s drain backoff:" >&2
  printf '%s\n' "$RERUN_TARGETS" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
  if [ "$BACKOFF" -gt 0 ]; then sleep "$BACKOFF"; fi
  BACKOFF=$((BACKOFF * 2))

  RETRY_CMD=()
  for arg in "${CMD[@]}"; do
    case "$arg" in
      --file-reporter=*) ;;            # rerun writes its own evidence log
      *) RETRY_CMD+=("$arg") ;;
    esac
  done

  SEGMENT="${CONSOLE}.rerun$RERUNS"
  REPORTER="${RETRY_LOG}.rerun$RERUNS"
  set +e
  "${RETRY_CMD[@]}" --file-reporter="json:$REPORTER" $RERUN_TARGETS 2>&1 \
    | tee "$SEGMENT" | tee -a "$CONSOLE"
  RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
  set -e
done

if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ "$RERUNS" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "✅ load-drop retry: healed — dropped file(s) green on rerun $RERUNS" >&2
  fi
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ load-drop retry: still red after $RERUNS rerun(s) (exit $RC) — failing loudly" >&2
exit "$RC"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# load_drop_retry.sh — bounded loopback-ws load-drop retry for sharded
# dart test legs (issue #2331).
#
# Family: under CI-leg load the dart test loader's loopback WebSocket
# (127.0.0.1:…/ws) to a freshly spawned test VM can die mid-handshake —
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection closed before full header was
